metadata.description: The ownership and isolation border. Every record's `tenant_uuid` resolves to one of these, and it is the referent that ownership, cost attribution, audit scope, drift accountability and policy scope all agree on. A member belongs to exactly one tenant at a time, structurally. Tenants nest: the child keeps its resources and its isolation, the parent holds governance overlay and rollup.

provider_ref.description: The auth-capability provider that evaluates this expression (cardinality-1 URF).

expression.description: OPAQUE provider-scoped subject expression — an LDAP DN, an OIDC claim, a K8s subject. Never parsed or evaluated by UDLM.

subject_bindings.description: External subject expressions whose holders this grouping is for: the RBAC bridge. Opaque by design; parsing or evaluating one would re-import the permission engine the model excludes.

membership_criterion.description: Always `estate?tenant_uuid=={self}`. A tenant's members are the records that state its uuid as their `tenant_uuid`, so tenancy is read from each record, never derived from other fields (#723, explicit tenancy).

obligations.description: Required here where the Base leaves it optional: a tenant IS an isolation border, so its isolation level is declared, and `none` is a deliberate statement. How a level is delivered (row-level security, separate stores, separate hardware) is the implementation's choice.

parent_group_uuid.description: The parent tenant this one nests inside; absent means a root tenant. A child keeps complete isolation — its resources never belong to the parent (GRP-INV-004) — while the parent holds governance overlay, cost rollup and audit aggregation. Destroying a parent requires resolving every child first; there is no cascade (GRP-INV-003).

context.purpose: The ownership and isolation border. Every record in the model carries a tenant_uuid pointing at one of these, and it is the referent that ownership, cost attribution, audit scope, drift accountability, and policy scope all resolve against.
context.plain_description: A tenant. A thing belongs to exactly one at a time, and that is a structural lock rather than a convention — crossing the border is a deliberate, recorded act, not a default. Tenants may nest: a child keeps its own resources and its own isolation, while the parent gets governance overlay, cost rollup, and audit aggregation across its children.
use_when: Something must have exactly one owner, and moving it between owners must be visible
You need a boundary that cost, audit, drift, and policy all agree on
You are modelling a business unit, a customer, or a team that owns infrastructure
not_for: Grouping without isolation — a cost centre, a project, a label. That is a plain Grouping, where a member may belong to many and enforcement is advisory
Deciding who may act — external RBAC owns that (ADR-008); this decides what belongs to whom
Permitting one tenant to use another's resources — that is Grouping.Authorization
works_with: Grouping.Authorization — the recorded exception that lets a relationship cross this border
Every estate record — tenant_uuid resolves here (TEN-001/003, [D3])
The governance matrix — isolation obligations are enforced over the derived member set
